analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines ~1370-1382): it adds a paragraph on the Qwen inline MTP assistant. The assistant speculates for one decode row; with more rows it runs ordinary decode that may chain, appends hidden rows to assistant history, stores a carry, and has two rollback env switches (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY). No code, endpoint, authorization, attestation, key custody or encryption control changes in this diff. The supplied units (head lines 1-797, the Nemotron Super and GLM5Next sections) are unchanged context and contain no changed lines. I did not see the patched lines in the supplied units, so I could not cite them directly.

Threat relevance: the described chained-history and carry state is assistant state kept in process memory. It touches T-028/T-041 (residual state and prefix-cache), A-001 (prompt data in memory), and TB-007 (inference engine). The text implies assistant history and carry are per-request. The supplied excerpt does not show that this state is isolated across requests or tenants, cleared at retirement, or included in prefix-cache checkpoints and cache-scope partitioning. The paragraph just after the patch says SSD recurrent reuse with a persistent MTP assistant needs a serializable checkpoint contract, which suggests the existing cache gates still apply. Because the code is not supplied, I record this as an unverified contract, not a finding. A later code review of EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift should check three things: carry and history isolation per request, release on cancel and retire, and consistency of speculation with the prefix-cache scope and the T-041 salt.

No security regression is evidenced by documentation-only changes. needs_deeper_review is set true only for the unseen implementation, which the corresponding code PR should cover.
